input: # What a repeated member name gives under `duplicates`. Only the
# TypeScript package has this option yet, so these rows are here and
# not in ../spec/ (see ../AGENTS.md, "Where a new fixture goes").
# 'merge' is the base grammars' own merge: two maps, member by member.
# It goes all the way down, and a third value merges into the first two.
# The case the option exists for: the operations of one path, written twice.
# Two lists merge index by index.
# Where the two are not both maps or both lists, the later value wins,
# The engine's merge leaves three names out of what it merges in:
# __proto__, constructor and prototype. A member so named in the first
# JSON text is read by the grammar under 'merge', whatever `fast` says:
# JSON.parse would keep the last value.
# 'last' is the default, spelled out: the last value, whole, on both paths.
# Under strict a repeated name is refused, whatever `duplicates` says.
